Which step of the engineering-design process is this? Students put their water filter to work and measure how clear the water comes out.
Checking results against goals is testing and evaluating.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? After the test, the team makes the wings of their glider longer so it flies farther.
Making changes based on test results is improving.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? A town needs a bridge that boats can still pass under.
Stating what the solution must do is defining the problem.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? Students vote on the best of their ideas for a bird feeder after listing many.
Generating and choosing among ideas is part of brainstorming.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? The class builds a cardboard model of a playground slide.
A model built to try out the idea is a prototype.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? Engineers put a new car seat in a crash-test sled and record the results.
A crash test checks how well the design works.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? The solar oven did not get hot enough, so students add foil to reflect more sunlight.
Adding foil after a poor result is improving the design.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? A team writes down that their robot must weigh under 2 kg and climb a ramp.
Criteria and constraints are set when defining the problem.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? Students make a mind map of ways to carry water without spilling.
A mind map of ideas is a brainstorming tool.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? The team builds a working small-scale wind turbine from wood and plastic.
Building a small working version is making a prototype.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? Students drop their parachute from a balcony and see if the egg survives.
Dropping the design to see if it works is testing.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? The tower fell over, so the team makes the base wider.
Widening the base after a failure is improving the design.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? Engineers find out that people in a village need a way to clean their drinking water.
Recognizing the need is the first step, defining the problem.
Which step of the engineering-design process is this? Students compare the results of three bridge tests to decide which held the most weight.
Comparing test results is evaluating the designs.
sciSciMeth: A student wonders, "Does salt make ice melt faster?" What step is this?
Wondering about something to investigate is asking a question.
A student predicts, "If I add salt, the ice will melt faster." What step is this?
A testable prediction is a hypothesis.
A student puts salt on one ice cube and nothing on another, then times them. What step is this?
Carrying out a test is doing an experiment.
A student writes down how many minutes each ice cube took to melt. What step is this?
Writing down measurements is recording observations or data.
A student makes a bar graph comparing the melting times. What step is this?
Organizing data into a graph helps analyze it.
A student says, "The salted ice melted faster, so my hypothesis was right." What step is this?
Deciding what the results mean is drawing a conclusion.
A student writes a report about the ice experiment for the class blog. What step is this?
Communicating findings to others is sharing results.
Which step comes right after asking a question?
After a question, scientists gather background information and make a hypothesis.
Which step comes right before drawing a conclusion?
You must look closely at the data before deciding what it means.
Scientists share their findings after drawing conclusions.
A final answer that cannot change
A hypothesis is an educated guess that can be tested.
In an experiment, what is the variable you change on purpose called?
The independent variable is the one the scientist changes.
In an experiment, what is the variable you measure called?
The dependent variable responds to the change and is measured.
Why do scientists keep all other variables the same in a test?
So it is a fair test
Keeping other variables constant means only one factor affects the results.
Why should an experiment be repeated several times?
To make sure the results are reliable
To change the hypothesis each time
Repeating trials shows whether results are consistent.
A student reads books and websites about plants before testing. What step is this?
Learning what is already known is background research.
A student grows one plant with fertilizer and one without. Which plant is the control?
The control group does not get the change being tested.
A student measures plant height with a ruler every day. What step is this?
Taking and writing down measurements is recording data.
A student's results do not match her hypothesis. What should she do?
Report it honestly and test a new hypothesis
Results that do not support a hypothesis are still useful and should be reported honestly.
A team presents a poster about their results at a science fair. What step is this?
Presenting findings to others is sharing results.
A student asks, "Which paper towel brand soaks up the most water?" Which is a good hypothesis?
If I test three brands, the thickest one will soak up the most water
A good hypothesis makes a testable prediction about the question.
A student finds the average of three trials. What step is this?
Calculating averages is part of analyzing data.

sciHeatFlow: You put your hand in cold lake water. Which way does heat flow?
From your hand to the water
From the water to your hand
Cold flows into your hand
Heat does not flow
Heat moves from the warmer hand to the colder water.
An ice cube sits in a glass of lemonade. Which way does heat flow?
From the lemonade to the ice cube
From the ice cube to the lemonade
Cold flows into the lemonade
Heat does not flow
The warmer lemonade gives heat to the colder ice.
A pot of water sits on a hot stove. Which way does heat flow?
From the stove to the pot
From the pot to the stove
Cold flows into the stove
Heat does not flow
Heat moves from the hot stove into the cooler pot.
You wrap your cold hands around a warm mug. Which way does heat flow?
From the mug to your hands
From your hands to the mug
Cold flows into the mug
Heat does not flow
The warmer mug transfers heat to your colder hands.
Frozen peas are put into hot boiling water. Which way does heat flow?
From the water to the peas
From the peas to the water
Cold flows into the water
Heat does not flow
Heat moves from the hot water to the frozen peas.
You touch a metal railing on a cold winter day. Which way does heat flow?
From your hand to the railing
From the railing to your hand
Cold flows into your hand
Heat does not flow
Your warmer hand loses heat to the cold metal.
A hot baked potato is wrapped in foil on the counter. Which way does heat flow?
From the potato to the surrounding air
From the air to the potato
Cold flows into the potato
Heat does not flow
The hot potato slowly loses heat to the cooler air.
Sun shines on a dark car seat. Which way does heat flow when you sit on the hot seat?
From the seat to your legs
From your legs to the seat
Cold flows into the seat
Heat does not flow
The hotter seat transfers heat to your cooler body.
You put a cold carton of milk into a warm room. Which way does heat flow?
From the room air to the milk
From the milk to the air
Cold flows into the room
Heat does not flow
The warmer air gives heat to the colder milk.
Two blocks touch: one at 60 °C and one at 20 °C. Which way does heat flow?
From the 60 °C block to the 20 °C block
From the 20 °C block to the 60 °C block
Both ways equally
Heat does not flow
Heat flows from higher temperature to lower temperature.
Two cups of water are both at 25 °C and touching. Which way does heat flow?
No net heat flows between them
From the left cup to the right cup
From the right cup to the left cup
Cold flows between them
Objects at the same temperature are in thermal equilibrium, so there is no net heat flow.
A snowball is held in a mitten-covered hand. Which way does heat flow?
From the hand through the mitten to the snowball
From the snowball to the hand
Cold flows from the snowball into the hand
Heat does not flow
Heat always travels from the warmer hand toward the colder snow.
A campfire warms your face. How does most of this heat reach you?
By radiation
By conduction
By convection only through the ground
Heat does not travel
Heat from a fire reaches you as infrared radiation through the air.
Hot air rises above a heater and cool air sinks to take its place. What kind of heat transfer is this?
Convection
Conduction
Radiation
Insulation
Convection moves heat by the flow of liquids or gases.
A metal pan handle gets hot when the pan is on the stove. What kind of heat transfer is this?
Conduction
Convection
Radiation
Evaporation
Conduction moves heat through direct contact within the metal.
Why does a wooden spoon stay cooler than a metal spoon in hot soup?
Wood is a poor conductor of heat
Wood is colder inside
Metal makes its own heat
Wood pushes cold into the soup
Wood is an insulator, so heat moves through it slowly.
Why does a winter coat keep you warm?
It slows heat flowing from your body to the cold air
It pushes cold out
It makes heat
It adds cold to the air
Insulating coats reduce heat loss from your body.
A cooler keeps drinks cold on a hot day. What does the cooler do?
Slows heat flowing from the warm air into the drinks
Makes cold
Pushes cold into the drinks
Stops time
Insulation slows heat transfer from the warmer outside.
A hot drink and a cold drink are mixed. What happens to the final temperature?
It ends up between the two starting temperatures
It becomes hotter than the hot drink
It becomes colder than the cold drink
It stays exactly the same as the hot drink
Heat flows from hot to cold until both reach a temperature in between.
A lizard lies on a warm rock in the morning. Which way does heat flow?
From the rock to the lizard
From the lizard to the rock
Cold flows from the lizard
Heat does not flow
The warmer rock heats the cooler lizard.
An ice pack is placed in a lunch bag with a sandwich. Which way does heat flow?
From the sandwich to the ice pack
From the ice pack to the sandwich
Cold flows from the ice pack into the sandwich
Heat does not flow
The ice pack keeps food cool by absorbing heat from it.
Hot soup is put in the fridge. Which way does heat flow?
From the soup to the cold fridge air
From the fridge air to the soup
Cold flows into the soup
Heat does not flow
The hot soup loses heat to the colder air in the fridge.
sciXsPredT: A glass of cold water sits in the sun. What will happen to its temperature?
The warm sunlight and air will heat the cold water.
A hot bowl of oatmeal sits on the table. What will happen to its temperature over time?
Heat moves from the oatmeal to the cooler air.
You put a warm bottle of water in the freezer. What will happen to its temperature?
The cold freezer air takes heat from the bottle.
A cold metal spoon is placed in hot cocoa. What happens to the spoon?
Heat flows from the hot cocoa into the spoon.
A frozen juice box is put in a lunch bag. What happens to the juice box by lunchtime?
The warmer air in the bag heats the frozen juice.
You hold an ice cube in your hand. What happens to your hand?
Your hand loses heat to the ice cube.
A warm cookie is placed on a cold plate. What happens to the plate?
Heat moves from the warm cookie into the colder plate.
Snow sits on a sidewalk on a warm, sunny spring day. What happens to the snow's temperature?
It turns to steam right away
The warm air and sun heat the snow until it melts.
A hot bath is left to sit for an hour. What happens to the water?
The bath water loses heat to the cooler room.
A cup of cold milk is left on the counter. What will its temperature become after many hours?
About the same as the room
Objects warm or cool until they match their surroundings.
A hot drink is poured into a foam cup and a thin metal cup. Which drink will cool faster?
The drink in the metal cup
The drink in the foam cup
They will cool at the same rate
Metal conducts heat away quickly, while foam is an insulator.
A cold apple is held in a warm hand. What happens to the apple?
Heat flows from the hand into the apple.
A pan is taken off a hot stove. What will happen to its temperature?
With no more heat from the stove, the pan cools in the air.
A thermometer reads 20 °C and is put into warm water at 40 °C. What will the thermometer show?
The thermometer warms up to match the warmer water.
A thermometer reads 22 °C and is put into a snowbank. What will the thermometer show?
The thermometer loses heat to the colder snow.
A cold stone is placed in a warm pond. What happens to the pond water right next to the stone?
The water gives some heat to the cold stone.
You wrap a hot potato in a towel. How does this change its cooling?
A towel insulates the potato, slowing heat loss.
A popsicle is taken out of the freezer. What happens to its temperature?
It drops below the freezer temperature
The warmer room air heats the popsicle.
A sunny window warms a cat lying beside it. What happens to the cat's fur temperature?
A metal slide sits in the sun all afternoon. What will its temperature be like?
Exactly the same as in the morning
Sunlight heats the metal throughout the afternoon.
A hot pie is set beside a cold pie. What happens to the cold pie?
It becomes hotter than the hot pie
Some heat flows from the hot pie to the cold pie.
Ice water is poured into a warm glass. What happens to the glass?
The glass loses heat to the colder ice water.
sciXsPCcmp: Toasting bread until it turns brown
Toasting makes new substances that give a brown colour and new smell.
Melted chocolate is still chocolate; only its state changed.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar to make bubbles
The bubbles are a new gas, carbon dioxide.
The sugar is still there and can be recovered by evaporating the water.
Heat changes the egg proteins into new substances that cannot go back.
A crushed can is still aluminum; only its shape changed.
An apple slice turning brown in air
Browning happens when substances in the apple react with oxygen.
Evaporation changes water from liquid to gas, but it is still water.
A copper roof turning green over time
The green coating is a new substance formed by reaction with air and water.
Pencil shavings are still wood and graphite.
Food being digested in your stomach
Digestion breaks food down into new substances.
Paper yellowing in sunlight over years
Folding changes only the shape of the paper.
Burning makes new substances, heat and light.
Ice cream melting on a hot day
Melted ice cream is still ice cream in liquid form.
Which is a clue that a chemical change has happened?
A new gas, colour or smell forms
The object is cut in half
The object is moved to a new place
New substances often give off gas, change colour or make a new smell.
Salt and pepper can be separated; no new substance is made.
Leaves rotting in a compost bin
Decomposition turns leaves into new substances like soil and gases.
A cake rising in the oven
Ice is still water; only its state changed.
Cake batter baking into a cake
Heat causes reactions that make new substances and gas bubbles.
The torn cloth is still the same material.
A glow stick lighting up when bent
Bending the stick mixes chemicals that react and give off light.
Grinding changes size only; the beans are still coffee.
sciFRC: Opening a door toward you by its handle
Bringing something toward you is a pull.
Pressing a button on an elevator
Pressing moves the button away from your finger, so it is a push.
Pulling a weed out of the garden
Lifting a weed toward you out of the soil is a pull.
Pushing a friend on a swing
Moving the swing away from you is a push.
Reeling brings the fish toward you, which is a pull.
Hitting a hockey puck with a stick
The stick moves the puck away, so it is a push.
Zipping up pulls the zipper along its track.
Moving the stroller ahead of you is a push.
Pulling a toboggan up a hill
Dragging the toboggan behind you is a pull.
Throwing moves the snowball away from you.
Drawing the curtain toward you is a pull.
The wheelbarrow moves ahead as you push it.
Earth's gravity making an apple fall
A dog tugging on its leash
The dog moves the leash toward itself, which is a pull.
Picking an apple from a tree
Pressing down moves the playdough away from your hand.
Picking an apple from a tree
You pull the apple off the branch toward you.
Pushing the ball down toward the floor makes it bounce.
Lifting a bucket by its handle
Pushing a box across the floor
Lifting a bucket by the handle pulls it up toward you.
Pushing a box across the floor
Moving the box away from you is a push.
Pulling on a pair of boots
Drawing the boots up onto your feet is a pull.
A bulldozer moving dirt in front of it
A tow truck towing a car
The bulldozer moves the dirt ahead of it, so it is a push.
